map_commands.controls_help:
SELECT — click an army or its commander portrait.
MARCH — click a reachable destination, or drag the army and release. Gold marks ordinary range; orange requires forced march (Shift). Red offers attack or siege, with battle confirmation.
JOURNEYS — M plans a route. A distant destination waits for Issue orders before the army sets out.
SCOUT — cavalry and spies see farther. Build a Watchtower in your territory, then fortify it for greater sight and defense. Scouting coverage shows the observed provinces.
INSPECT — Alt-click a province, or deselect with Esc first. Right-click a unit row for its card.
CAMERA — drag empty land, middle-drag or Space-drag; WASD/arrows pan, wheel/pinch or +/- zoom. F finds the selected force; V changes map detail; Home returns to the capital.
FLEETS — select a fleet and right-click a sea to sail, or your port to dock.
OPTIONS — play or skip the turn sequence; guided objectives; reduced motion.
map_commands.welcome_controls: Click a commander or army, then click a destination to march. Drag the army to preview its road. Space-drag pans; Alt-click inspects. Options ▾ lists all controls.
map_commands.idle_controls: Click an army or commander to select it, then click a gold destination to march. Orange requires forced march; red offers attack or siege.
map_commands.map_intro: Command from the land your scouts have charted. Roads, passes and bridges determine the march; terrain determines the defense.
map_commands.uncharted: Uncharted territory. Send scouts or negotiate access to another court’s maps.
map_commands.map_access_help: Includes their atlas and future geographic reports. Live troop intelligence stays separate. War ends future updates.
map_commands.chart_known: Remembered countryside. This view retains the last survey; troops and new construction require fresh observation.
map_commands.frontier_help: Dark ground is uncharted. Maps can be exchanged through diplomacy.
map_commands.patrol_help: Spend {cost} movement to search this province and {radius} connected border. Forest contacts stay revealed until the next season. No battle is started.
map_commands.patrol_need_army: Select your army to send a patrol.
map_commands.patrol_no_movement: The column lacks movement for a woodland patrol.
map_commands.patrol_siege: Lift the siege before sending a woodland patrol.
map_commands.patrol_done: Patrols have searched the nearby woods. Reports last through this season; {cost} movement spent.
map_commands.forest_warning: Woodland can hide troops. Mounted scouts, nearby spies or forts, and Patrol woods reveal them; maps alone do not.
map_commands.forest_description: Normal columns in woodland evade distant lookouts. A local army, agent or tower, nearby mounted scouts, spies or forts, or a paid patrol reveals them. Forced marching and besieging expose troops.
map_commands.route_brief: Lead this column from Pannonia’s woods across the Illyrian bridge, Venetia’s marsh causeway and the Noric–Raetian passes. Choose each waypoint, then issue its march. End turn restores movement. At Noreia, Patrol woods searches the neighbouring forest. Orders, diplomacy and saves work normally.
map_commands.route_current: Current position: {region} · Select the column, then choose a waypoint.
map_commands.route_concealment: FOREST RECONNAISSANCE · Distant lookouts see land, not troops. Patrol woods costs {cost} movement; nearby mounted scouts, spies and forts also penetrate cover.
map_commands.route_saved: Alpine Route saves are separate from the full campaign.
map_commands.route_menu_help: A Julii route through forests, bridges and mountain passes. Separate saves.
map_commands.main_menu_confirm: Return to the main menu? Unsaved progress will be lost. Cancel and press Save first to keep it.

map_commands.countryside_help: Inspect terrain, roads and nearby settlements.

map_commands.enter_city_help: Visit Roma’s streets and governing offices.
map_commands.city_zoom_help: Scroll to inspect the city; continue outward to the countryside.
map_commands.report_remembered: Last observed in season {turn} · {age} seasons ago. Buildings and ownership may have changed.
map_commands.report_geography: Charted terrain only. No settlement survey is available.
map_commands.report_forest: Forest cover can hide troops even in observed territory. Local scouts, patrols and watchposts provide detection.

city_view.menu_help: Govern the city, train its garrison and command its defense. The campaign travels with you.
city_view.title: R O M A   /   THE LIVING CITY
city_view.subtitle: Governor’s district
city_view.welcome: Roma is your seat of government. City, army and campaign share one treasury and history.

city_view.govern_help: Orders affect the people and treasury of this district. Civic days advance local work and sentiment; campaign seasons advance separately. Walking takes no simulation time.
city_view.esc_close: Choose an order or review a building’s development · Esc closes this panel
city_view.click_walk: Click the street to walk  ·  W A S D to move  ·  Esc to release the cursor
city_view.walking: Mouse to look · Click to select · Right-click to inspect · Tab / Esc for the pointer

city_view.refused: This order cannot be carried out. Check the treasury and current orders.
city_view.day_passed: A civic day has passed. Work, provisions and public sentiment have been updated.
city_view.saved: Roma saved. Your city uses its own save slot.
city_view.save_failed: Could not save Roma. Your previous save is retained.
city_view.loaded: Roma restored. Walk the district to see the saved conditions.
city_view.load_failed: No compatible Roma save could be loaded.
city_view.about_forum: Citizens gather here to trade news and petition their governor. A restless crowd reveals pressures that patrols alone cannot resolve.
city_view.about_curia: Issue orders from the council house. Lower burdens, fund improvements, or strengthen the watch; each choice spends money or changes the people’s consent.
city_view.about_barracks: Walk through the gate into the muster yard, inspect the soldiers and enter the quarters. More patrols make authority visible, but enforced order carries a social cost.
city_view.about_tavern: Step through the doorway for wine, benches, pottery and neighborhood gossip. Closing the tavern disperses its patrons while increasing their resentment.
city_view.about_market: Stalls and grain queues bring the district’s daily needs into view. Temporary relief reduces immediate hardship and costs the treasury.
city_view.about_fountain: Public water and the surrounding drains need upkeep. Fund repairs here and let the workers finish before expecting an improvement.
city_view.help_grain_relief: Fund a temporary supply of grain. A queue appears at the market; relief lowers pressure while supplies last.
city_view.help_patrols_increase: More soldiers patrol the streets. Daily upkeep rises and coercion adds grievance over time.
city_view.help_patrols_reduce: Reduce the visible watch and its daily expense. The underlying causes of unrest remain.
city_view.help_tax_low: Lower the settlement tax rate and subsidize the district each civic day. Consent improves gradually.
city_view.help_tax_normal: Return the settlement to its ordinary tax rate and district upkeep.
city_view.help_tax_high: Raise the settlement tax rate and reduce the daily civic subsidy. Burden builds resentment.
city_view.help_repair_streets: Pay a work crew to repair damaged paving. The crew remains until the project finishes after several civic days.
city_view.help_clean_water: Fund cleaning and repairs. Refuse clears and water improves when the work is complete.
city_view.help_close_taverns: Shutter the tavern and disperse its patrons. Visible gatherings decline, but grievance rises.
city_view.help_reopen_taverns: Lift the restriction. Patrons return and the extra grievance from closure stops accumulating.
city_view.reason_unauthorized: This city belongs to another faction.
city_view.reason_unsupported_city: This city does not yet support local campaign management.
city_view.reason_insufficient_funds: The treasury cannot cover this expense.
city_view.reason_project_active: The workers are already on this task.
city_view.city.dialogue.citizen.calm: The fountain is busy this morning. I hope the water stays clear.
city_view.city.dialogue.citizen.restive: We pay, and still the street outside our door goes untended.
city_view.city.dialogue.citizen.rebellious: We came to be heard. The governor must answer for these burdens.
city_view.city.dialogue.merchant.calm: Come closer. Grain, olives and good oil for your household.
city_view.city.dialogue.merchant.restive: Customers count every coin now. So do I.
city_view.city.dialogue.merchant.rebellious: Trade cannot thrive while the whole square is arguing.
city_view.city.dialogue.porter.calm: Another load for the market. Mind the cart tracks.
city_view.city.dialogue.porter.restive: My shoulders carry the sacks; my household carries the taxes.
city_view.city.dialogue.porter.rebellious: There is work everywhere, and too little left for our families.
city_view.city.dialogue.guard.calm: The watch is making its rounds. Keep the roadway clear.
city_view.city.dialogue.guard.restive: We can disperse a crowd. We cannot fill its stomachs.
city_view.city.dialogue.guard.rebellious: Orders are orders. But these are our neighbors in the square.
city_view.city.dialogue.patron.calm: Sit a while. There is bread, wine and news from the market.
city_view.city.dialogue.patron.restive: Everyone here has a complaint. Listen before you judge us.
city_view.city.dialogue.patron.rebellious: Shutting a door will not silence what people say outside it.
city_view.city.dialogue.protester.calm: We have brought a petition. Hear what the district needs.
city_view.city.dialogue.protester.restive: Less burden. Clean water. We have asked for both.
city_view.city.dialogue.protester.rebellious: We will stay in the square until someone listens.
city_view.city.dialogue.grain_queue.calm: This provision gives our household a little breathing room.
city_view.city.dialogue.grain_queue.restive: We are grateful for the grain. What happens when it runs out?
city_view.city.dialogue.grain_queue.rebellious: One distribution will not undo everything we have endured.

city_view.project_terms: Investment %d denarii · %d civic days · upkeep %d per day
city_view.residence_about: A private household and its street frontage. The governor can improve the shared streets and water supply, and change the burdens borne by the people living here.
city_view.residence_evolution: Public paving and water works improve conditions outside these homes. Private rebuilding is not yet available; civic orders below affect the district as a whole.
city_view.reason_unknown_site: This place has no civic ledger.
city_view.help_improve_tavern: Repair the frontage and add shaded seating. A more comfortable gathering place gradually eases grievance; keeping it maintained costs money.
city_view.help_improve_barracks: Provide better stores, equipment racks and an orderly muster frontage. The stronger institution builds trust, while closer official scrutiny adds some grievance.
city_view.help_improve_market: Add covered trading space and better provision stalls. More reliable trade eases grievance and builds trust, with daily maintenance to pay.
city_view.help_improve_curia: Repair the civic frontage and improve the public notice area. Visible, dependable administration builds trust; the work and its upkeep draw on the treasury.
city_view.stage_forum_current: Weathered paving and worn edges leave the central gathering place in need of attention.
city_view.stage_forum_construction: Stonemasons stage new paving and mark the work area. The square remains accessible while the order progresses.
city_view.stage_forum_improved: Repaired paving replaces damaged stretches. Its upkeep becomes a standing commitment, and the district benefits from less disrepair.
city_view.stage_fountain_current: The public water point serves the neighborhood, but dirty surroundings and worn drains diminish its usefulness.
city_view.stage_fountain_construction: The water and drainage work is funded. Its benefits arrive when the workers complete the project.
city_view.stage_fountain_improved: Cleaner water and cleared surroundings improve sanitation. Maintenance is charged each day to sustain the service.
city_view.stage_tavern_current: A modest food-and-wine shop serves the neighborhood from a worn frontage. Licensing determines whether patrons may gather.
city_view.stage_tavern_construction: Scaffolding marks the funded refit. Workers prepare the frontage and shaded seating while the civic days pass.
city_view.stage_tavern_improved: A renewed frontage and shaded seating make the tavern a more comfortable social place. Licensing still controls whether it may open.
city_view.stage_barracks_current: The muster house holds basic quarters, weapons and supplies around an open drill yard.
city_view.stage_barracks_construction: The funded refit adds ordered stores and a better frontage. The garrison continues to occupy its existing quarters.
city_view.stage_barracks_improved: Additional equipment displays, stores and civic colors show the stronger institution. Maintaining it costs money, and closer authority has a social cost.
city_view.stage_market_current: Open provision stalls expose vendors and their goods to the weather. Grain relief, when ordered, draws a distribution queue.
city_view.stage_market_construction: Scaffolds and materials mark the expansion of covered trading space. Benefits begin when the project finishes.
city_view.stage_market_improved: Covered stalls and renewed trading furniture support a more dependable market. Relief remains a separate temporary order.
city_view.stage_curia_current: The council house receives petitions and issues district orders from a plainly maintained civic frontage.
city_view.stage_curia_construction: Workers restore the administrative frontage and prepare an improved public notice area.
city_view.stage_curia_improved: Restored finishes and a formal notice area make civic authority visible. The improvement strengthens trust and requires continuing upkeep.
city_view.preview_notice: 3D study · Drag to rotate. Previewing this stage does not order or complete work.

city_view.troops_help: The formations drilling in the town are your actual garrison. Recruit foot soldiers, archers or cavalry here; completed training and equipment programmes carry into battle.
city_view.troops_gain: On completion · experience +%d · weapons +%d · armour +%d (campaign caps apply)
city_view.troops_queued: Queued %s in the campaign muster roster.
city_view.troops_standalone: Recruitment is paid in money and population. The first cohort trains over three civic days, then joins the visible town garrison.
city_view.troops_season_note: Recruit here or on the campaign map. Civic training also progresses as seasons pass.
city_view.troops_none: No eligible companies are stationed here.
city_view.dawn_subtitle: A new morning in Roma. These are the consequences of the day just resolved.
city_view.dawn_expenses: Orders already paid: %d denarii · Civic upkeep paid overnight: %d denarii
city_view.dawn_cause_note: These daily flows change accumulated sentiment. Patrols, provisions and repairs also affect visible unrest directly. Stock limits can cap the final change. Newly completed works affect the following day’s flows.
city_view.dawn_no_report: Resolve a civic day to receive the first morning report.
city_view.work_rate: Current crews deliver %d units of building work per civic day. Troop programmes keep their own training pace.
city_view.help_drill_maniples: Requires the restored barracks. After three civic days, recruitable land units present in Roma’s garrison gain one experience level. Future recruits raised here receive one additional level, within the campaign cap. Instructors cost upkeep; duty adds grievance.
city_view.help_equip_maniples: Requires the completed drill programme. After four civic days, eligible land units present in Roma’s garrison receive improved weapons and armour through the campaign’s equipment rules. New recruits and eligible units refitted here receive the same standard. Stores require ongoing upkeep.
city_view.reason_project_required: Complete the preceding barracks programme first.
city_view.reason_under_siege: Military work is suspended while Roma is under siege.
city_view.reason_insufficient_population: The settlement cannot spare enough recruits.
city_view.reason_unit_unavailable: This troop type cannot currently be recruited in Roma.
city_view.event_relief_expired: The last grain ration was distributed. Relief must be renewed to continue.
city_view.help_workforce_normal: Ordinary crews complete one work day per civic day, with no additional labor subsidy. Military training always keeps its own pace.
city_view.help_workforce_paid: Pay for additional crews to complete two work days per civic day. Daily subsidy increases and fair employment slowly builds trust. Military training is unchanged.
city_view.help_workforce_requisition: Compel households to supply labor, completing two work days per civic day with a smaller subsidy. Grievance rises and trust falls. Military training is unchanged.
city_view.troops_recruited: New troops have joined the town garrison.
city_view.troops_counters: Archers counter cavalry; cavalry counter foot soldiers; foot soldiers counter archers.
city_view.calendar_help: Stay in Roma while the Mediterranean changes around it. Each season resolves taxes, upkeep, growth, construction and other factions. City work also progresses. A siege or an important decision interrupts a longer advance.
city_view.calendar_civic: Each season schedules %d civic work days. Individual civic days remain available for close management; they do not move the campaign calendar.
city_view.calendar_span: Campaign era: %s to %s. Your recorded history follows the seasons you actually play.
city_view.calendar_passed: %d seasons passed · %d civic work days completed.
city_view.calendar_history_empty: The first seasonal advance begins the city record.
city_view.calendar_annals_empty: No events have yet been recorded here.
city_view.calendar_unfunded: Some civic work could not be funded; seasonal revenue and upkeep still resolved.
city_view.calendar_lost: Roma is no longer under your control. Continue from the campaign map.
city_view.calendar_busy: Resolve or close the battle before advancing the campaign.
city_view.reason_not_owner: Roma is no longer yours to govern.
city_view.reason_diplomacy: An envoy awaits your answer on the campaign map.
city_view.reason_campaign_finished: This campaign has reached its conclusion.
city_view.reason_winner: This campaign has reached its conclusion.
city_view.reason_invalid_region: This city does not support local campaign management.
city_view.shared_save_failed: The campaign could not be saved. Your session remains open.
city_view.menu_resume_roma: CONTINUE IN ROMA · One living campaign
city_view.reason_decision_pending: An envoy or the Senate awaits your answer on the campaign map.
city_view.reason_nearby_threat: A hostile army is approaching Roma.
city_view.menu_resume_campaign_help: Resume your shared save. Enter Roma from the campaign map when the city is yours.
city_view.defense_help: Walk the curtain wall, examine the gate and review the barracks. Fund improvements here; completed work carries into the next siege. Inspection does not advance time.
city_view.defense_gate_help: The timber gate is the first breach point. Reinforcement adds %d integrity to the next siege. Unfinished work grants no protection.
city_view.defense_curtain_help: Prepare incendiary arrows for your archers. Repeated volleys can ignite the exposed timber of the siege ram. Fire consumes the ram until it is destroyed.
city_view.defense_barracks_help: Inspect the yard and quarters, recruit archers, drill the garrison and improve its equipment before the assault.
city_view.help_reinforce_gate: Fit cross-bracing and iron straps. The next siege begins with a stronger gate. Labour and upkeep increase the civic burden.
city_view.help_prepare_fire_arrows: Equip the archers with prepared fire arrows for exposed siege timber. Requires upkeep; construction crews add to civic strain.
city_view.defense_locked: Inspection remains available; defense work cannot begin during a siege.

city_battle.title: Defence of Roma
city_battle.subtitle: Deploy your garrison. Then command the battle as it unfolds.
city_battle.briefing: Command a continuous battle in Roma. Deploy, manoeuvre, shoot, charge and hold the Forum.
city_battle.practice_help: Fight with a copy of the actual garrison. Recruited troops and training appear here; practice losses do not alter the town.
city_battle.live_help: A live defence uses the actual besieging army and garrison. Casualties and the result apply to the campaign when the battle ends.
city_battle.command_help: Right-click ground to move, or an enemy to focus attacks. Choose an order for the selected troops.
city_battle.deployment_help: Select troops, then right-click any clear street or square to deploy. Begin battle when ready.

city_battle.reason_wrong_phase: That command is unavailable in this battle phase.
city_battle.reason_battle_unfinished: Finish this campaign battle before clearing its report.
city_battle.reason_defense_pending: Resolve Roma’s pending defence before advancing the campaign.
city_battle.counters: Archers counter cavalry. Cavalry counter foot soldiers. Foot soldiers counter archers. Training, numbers and positioning still matter.
city_battle.reason_invalid_position: Choose a clear street or square. Buildings and closed walls block movement.
city_battle.reason_no_path: That position cannot be reached from here.
city_battle.camera_help: Camera: WASD pan · wheel zoom · middle-drag pan · Alt-drag orbit · F follow · V aerial
city_battle.selection_help: Drag to select · Shift adds · right-click orders · right-drag places a frontage
city_battle.camera_plan_help: Double-click or middle-drag the plan to move the camera.
city_battle.reason_fire_unprepared: Prepare incendiary arrows during peacetime first.
city_battle.reason_archers_only: Select only archer cohorts for this order.
city_battle.reason_no_engine: There is no surviving siege ram.
city_battle.siege_help: Deploy archers near the south gate to reach the ram. Use Target siege ram, then fire arrows if prepared. Ordinary arrows damage its crew and equipment.
city_battle.ability_commander_help: For %d s, unobstructed friendly troops within %d m gain %d morale and take %d%% less damage. The escort also deals %d%% more damage. Ready again %d s after activation. Does not restore casualties or rally already routed troops.
city_battle.ability_veteran_help: For %d s, deal %d%% more damage and gain %d morale. Ready again %d s after activation.
city_battle.ability_spear_guard_help: For %d s, take %d%% less damage, cancel cavalry charge bonuses and gain %d morale. Movement slows to %d%%. Ready again %d s after activation.
city_battle.reason_no_ability: Select a general’s guard or specialist formation with a special ability.
city_battle.reason_ability_recovering: That formation’s special ability is still recovering.
city_battle.ability_help: Select one specialist formation to use its ability. Abilities can be ordered while paused; their timers advance only with the battle.
city_battle.ability_legacy: Abilities become available in newly started battles.
city_battle.tactics_help: Right-drag across clear ground to place a frontage and facing. Troops move there together; use Attack move to assault along the way. Face direction then right-click to guard an approach.
city_battle.phalanx_help: Requires phalanx-trained spears and experience %d. Forming takes %d s. Frontal attack +%d%%, frontal damage taken −%d%%, speed %d%%. Slow turning; flanks and cavalry behind the line are dangerous. Needs room for locked shields.
city_battle.column_help: Narrow marching ranks move faster but take more damage. Change to battle line before contact.
city_battle.split_help: Divide one unengaged battalion into three independently commanded platoons. Strength, losses and recovery are conserved; survivors reunite after battle. General guards remain together.
city_battle.reason_no_tactics: Formation orders are available in newly started battles.
city_battle.reason_phalanx_training: Select phalanx-capable spears with sufficient experience.
city_battle.reason_formation_space: There is not enough clear ground for that formation or frontage.
city_battle.reason_cannot_split: Select one unsplit battalion with enough troops, away from melee. General guards cannot split.
city_battle.reason_reforming: Wait for these troops to finish changing formation.
city_battle.frontage_hint: Release to place the frontage · arrow shows facing
city_battle.drill_help: Practice with trained hoplites, cavalry and archers. Split platoons, place assault frontages and guard your flanks. This drill uses supplied troops and has no campaign cost or reward.

waterways.title: Waterways & shipping
waterways.intro: Develop ports and shipyards to improve transport, trade and fleet strength. Voyage orders continue each season.
waterways.port_hint: Use Port development to expand the waterfront and commission vessels.
waterways.capacity: Passengers: {used}/{capacity} soldiers, including commanders; crew is separate.
waterways.trade_paused: paused — access, port or war interruption
waterways.trade_note: Freight income is limited by ship capacity and both ports. One delivery is paid per season; lost access pauses service.
waterways.voyage_issued: Voyage to {destination} issued; unused legs resume next season.
waterways.invalid: This waterway order is unavailable. Check movement, access, capacity and port requirements.
waterways.landing_required: Build a landing or port first.
waterways.cargo_aboard: Land troops before regrouping, trading or docking.
waterways.route_unavailable: No navigable route for these ships.
waterways.no_access: Both riverbanks must be owned to build a bridge.
waterways.not_ready: This project is already built or queued, or funds are insufficient.
waterways.no_movement: Not enough movement remains this season.
waterways.capacity_error: This fleet lacks space for the whole army.
waterways.occupied: The landing is blocked, besieged, or hostile.
waterways.wrong_owner: Only your own fleets and troops can receive orders.
waterways.battle_active: Finish the current battle before issuing campaign orders.
waterways.fleet_hint: Choose a distant waterway and issue a voyage, or right-click a waterway on the map. Right-click a shore to land carried troops; empty fleets dock at owned ports.
waterways.beach: Land troops on the shore at {name}
waterways.handling_full: This port has used its troop handling allowance for this season.
waterways.cargo_empty: These ships have no freight capacity.

ports.title: Port development
ports.intro: Expand the waterfront, specialize its facilities, then commission ships. Inland ports remain part of the river network.
ports.capabilities:
Troop handling {troops}/season · freight {cargo}/delivery
Repair {repair}% on {support} hulls/season · harbor defense +{defense}%
Port maintenance {upkeep} denarii/season
ports.gallery_note: Development preview with eligible specialist facilities. Previewing does not construct buildings or unlock ships.
ports.geometry_note: Shared footprints mark quays, obstacles, gates and berths. Traversal and tactical port battles are future phases.
ports.ship_required: A suitable port and vessel blueprint are required.
ports.no_water: This province has no authored waterway access.
ports.besieged: The port is besieged; work and servicing are suspended.
ports.population: The settlement cannot supply the required crew.
ports.stage_required: Develop the port to the required stage.
ports.deep_required: This vessel requires a deep-water coastal site.
ports.water_required: This vessel cannot operate on the waters at this site.
ports.busy: A waterfront project is already underway.
ports.complete: The waterfront has reached its final stage.
ports.handling_full: This port has used its troop handling allowance for this season.
ports.wrong_owner: Only the owner can develop this port.
ports.battle_active: Finish the active battle before changing the port.
ports.cargo_empty: These ships have no freight capacity.
ports.repair_note: Repair is paid and capped per season. Advanced hulls need a repair yard. Dock and land passengers before servicing.
ports.camera: Drag to orbit · scroll to zoom · Shift-drag to pan
